messages:
Ajay: Hey team — ETAHealth on Dedicated reported a tail latency regression after the last kernel shuffle. Can we triage?
Maria: saw the alert this morning, p95 up ~30ms for seq<=128 requests on their pool.
Lucas: I pulled a quick profile: kernel changed to `cu80-opt-v2` last night. Profile summary: kernel=cu80-opt-v2, seq_len_dist=[32:45%,64:30%,128:25%], avg_batch=5.8, p50=38ms, p95=220ms, kv_hit=0.78.
Kelly: interesting — kv_hit dropped from ~0.88 -> 0.78? that could explain extra fetch cost. any cache eviction churn?
Maria: yes, KV cache eviction rate spiked when the new kernel switched batching alignment, message from profiler: `kv_evictions_per_min: 120 -> 380`.
Ajay: so two things: kernel kernel selection changed batch packing and reduced effective prefix reuse, + higher evictions -> more KV loads. That amplifies p95.
Lucas: attached quick flame: `cpu_kv_io` jumps on small-batch tail. Suggests we should favor slightly larger target_batch formation for this pool and increase token_budget to allow grouping.
Kelly: etahealth requests a customer-specific token_budget bump. Their current config: `token_budget: 60k`, `max_queue_len: 150`. They want lower latency, but currently they get higher tail.
Ajay: proposal for a targeted canary: bump token_budget -> 120k, max_queue_len -> 250, and set `target_batch_ms: 12` (was 8). Also enable kv_prefetch for this pool for 10m window. Quick config snippet:```
dedicated_pools:
  etahealth-prod:
    token_budget: 120000
    max_queue_len: 250
    target_batch_ms: 12
    kv_prefetch: true
```
Maria: +1 but with guard rails: canary 5% traffic for 30m, monitor p50/p95, kv_hit, evictions, and queue_length. rollback if p95 > 240ms or kv_evictions not falling.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for `etahealth-prod` pool (5% traffic) — logs: https://deploys.redwood/etahealth/1832502
Lucas: quick simulated perf after proposed config (local replay): avg_batch -> 8.1, p50=34ms, p95=160ms, kv_hit=0.86, tokens/slice throughput +18%.
Kelly: good numbers. we should also patch the kernel selector to prefer the older kernel variant for seq<=128 until we finish kernel tuning. Can we add a routing override?
Ajay: yes — runtime policy supports model_kernel_overrides per-pool. I'll create an override: `prefer: cu80-opt-v1` for seq<=128 during canary. That avoids changing global rollout.
Maria: action items: Ajay will push pool config + kernel override to canary, Lucas will run replay and provide perf artifacts, Kelly will coordinate with SRE to watch alerts, I'll message ETAHealth CS with timeline.
Ajay: pushing change now. CLI diff:```
PATCH /api/dedicated/pools/etahealth-prod
{
  "token_budget": 120000,
  "max_queue_len": 250,
  "target_batch_ms": 12,
  "kernel_override": {"seq_max": 128, "prefer": "cu80-opt-v1"},
  "kv_prefetch": true
}
```
runtime-bot: config applied to canary group (5% traffic).
deploy-bot: Canary metrics snapshot: p50=36ms (+2ms), p95=162ms (-58ms), avg_batch=7.9, kv_hit=0.85, kv_evictions_per_min=95. No error spike.
Lucas: artifacts uploaded: replay traces + flamegraphs: https://perf.redwood/etahealth/1832502. Key takeaway: increasing token_budget allowed batch formation to stabilize, and kernel override prevented the small-batch regression.
Kelly: recommend we hold for 2 hours and then roll to 50% if metrics stable. also schedule a ticket for kernel selector tuning and a runtime improvement to detect kv_eviction spikes and auto-suggest token_budget changes.
Maria: agreed. ETAHealth CS notified.
Ajay: I'll follow up with a short note in #customer-success once we hit 50% roll and again on full rollout. Closing loop: will revert override after we finish kernel-side fix and re-run quant bench.
Kelly: thanks everyone. follow-up: open a small RFC for `adaptive_token_budget` heuristic? seems warranted.
Ajay: filed RFC #1492 for adaptive_token_budget.
Maria: closing thread for now. ping here if any regression during rollouts.
